action_summary: A software repair was reported as done while the file it named was byte-identical and its own stated test still failed. Measured on c79a8f5 with 18 human software-engineering sentences against fresh trees and a filesystem oracle: 1/18 solved, and the single repair-class PASS was false. Six wiring defects, each reusing machinery the repository already owns: the shared PYTHONPATH helper gave a suite the source file's own directory instead of the package's import root; the derivation built an argv that executes the test FILE instead of collecting it; the apply capability's in-place gate ran the stated test with no import path at all; the iterative loop used the test's path instead of the sources'; a repair sentence was answered by a read-only mechanism that restores the source and still returned PASS; and one executed failure closed the question so a decisive typed capability was never tried. After: 7/18 PASS, every one verified by the filesystem, repair across flat / pkg / src-app / app layouts 4/4, and zero repair PASSes with an unchanged source.

prior_work_reused.what: PR #6282 established that a tie between a capability that acts and one that only reads must not be settled in the reader's favour, and #6272 established that a template must not demand what the adapter defaults. This PR applies the same rule to the five inputs that made the scaffold unbindable.

PR #6272 made solve() catch SystemExit, which is what turned this capability's _fail() -- a sys.exit carrying a JSON reason -- into a readable FAIL_CLOSED__CAPABILITY_EXITED_PROCESS instead of a dead caller during measurement.

route_frontier.negative_search_summary: Widening the make...upper window from 20 to 200 characters was rejected as the same rule with a bigger number: it would still be a distance, it would still be wrong for a long enough path, and it would widen every sentence the window was keeping out. Masking the operand is what the blank arm in the same block already does, so this reuses a mechanism rather than inventing one. Adding 'not' to `_NEGATED_LINE` itself was rejected: that pattern is scoped to contain/match/include and is used by the VALUE arms, so widening it would invert value questions nobody measured. Inverting on the bare word 'not' was rejected -- 'the lines that are not blank' and 'the lines that are not sorted' are different questions and only the first is about blankness, so the negation is anchored to blank|empty. Fixing all 13 window-shaped rules at once was rejected as unmeasured: only the one that produced a certified wrong answer was fixed, and the rest are recorded as an open item with their count rather than being changed on suspicion. All alternatives DISQUALIFIED on measured grounds.

measured: _MUTATING_POSTCONDITIONS held cp, mkdir, mv, rm and touch, and tee fell through to the not-re-runnable branch

measured after: 14 of 14 everyday commands exact-verified with measured false passes at zero -- tee, rm, cp, mv, mkdir, touch, cat, wc, sort, head, grep, nl, sha256sum and a quoted stated write each carry a verifier pass=True
measured: the bytes on disk equal the digest the producer fingerprinted, so existence is not the only tie between the file and the command

measured and rejected: asserting the file is empty would be a claim about stdin, which the argv shape never observes -- so the promise is claimed at the strength tee guarantees unconditionally and no further
BROAD_WEB_OR_COMMUNITY: https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=postcondition%20verify%20effect%20not%20rerun -- a mutating command is verified by the state it left, never by running it twice; no standalone project owns the rule because it is a property of the check
CODE_OR_PACKAGE_REGISTRY: https://pypi.org/pypi/astunparse/json and the standard library's own compile() error handling -- both treat a parse failure as a property of one input rather than a fatal condition for the caller
OFFICIAL_PRIMARY: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/tee.html -- tee opens its operand with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, which is what makes the operand's existence a promise independent of its input

tournament.decisive_question: Does a sentence that asks for the tests to be run reach a capability that runs them, and does the measurement then tell a passing suite from a failing one -- without altering any argv token that is not a validated test path?
tournament.no_known_counterexample_reason: Each direction was falsified directly. test_a_passing_suite_that_imports_its_sibling_module_exits_zero and test_a_failing_suite_that_imports_its_sibling_module_still_exits_nonzero pin the suite runner from both sides. test_a_supplied_argv_naming_the_test_by_its_repo_relative_path_measures_it and test_a_failing_suite_supplied_the_same_way_is_still_measured_as_failing pin the argv rewrite from both sides, and test_it_matches_the_measurement_taken_when_no_argv_is_supplied requires the two routes to agree. test_an_argument_that_is_not_a_test_path_passes_through_verbatim is the nearest world in which the rewrite must not fire: the interpreter, -c and a whole harness program must come back untouched and only the test token may change. test_a_stated_test_that_already_passes_is_reported_truthfully_and_nothing_is_written asserts applied False, files_written empty and the source bytes unchanged.
